newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Asia welcomes change in LIFFE coffee contract. [CORRECTED 15:40 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Asia welcomes change in LIFFE coffee contract. [CORRECTED 15:40 GMT]

text.p: Asian coffee producers welcomed changes to the robusta coffee contract on the London International Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE), officials said on Thursday.

"Among the trade in the Far East I think they welcomed the changes because what we are trying to do is to create, perhaps, a more level playing field for coffee from the region," Joanne Shannon, Product Development Manager for Coffee in LIFFE, told Reuters during an Asia coffee conference here.

LIFFE announced last March that it would implement, starting from the July 1997 delivery month, a regrading of coffee and introduce a defect count for mouldy beans. But a move to introduce a maximum moisture content requirement had been put off until further notice.
(Corrects to delete reference to maximum moisture content requirement being introduced.)
"We've introduced a defect count," Shannon continued. "There was none before."
Doan Trieu Nhan, vice chairman of Vinacafe, said the changes were welcome and would boost the profile of Asian origin coffee.
The last two changes were introduced partly because of concerns among Far East traders and end users in developed countries about the quality of coffee beans from Asia.
"The changes in LIFFE's robusta contract will not pose any problems for Indonesian coffee," a representative from an Indonesian coffee trading house said.
